The body obtains float attributes for selectors 0x1e, 0x40, and 0x16; it combines 0x40 with the other two values, divides the resulting sums, then maps the ratio to return codes 0 through 5 at explicit thresholds. It returns -2 on invalid provider/context. The indexed caller passes the provider and stores the returned code, without establishing a more specific game-domain meaning.

Corrected because the first selector is supplied dynamically in the third argument (copied from c->x[2]); the body reads that selector plus fixed selector 0x11. It computes a derived metric and maps thresholds 9, 19, ..., 99 to result codes 0 through 10, with -2 for null input. The proposed label’s general quantization/result behavior is sound, but “player attribute value” implies a single direct value and misses the dynamic selector-derived metric. The caller passes its selector in x2 and stores the returned code; no domain meaning is proven.
